Title: Three rescued, woman missing in Ipoh water surge
Article:
IPOH: A 21-year-old woman is feared drowned after being swept away by strong currents during a sudden surge of water at Puncak Jelapang Waterfall in Meru Raya today.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department Operations Division assistant director Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said a team from the Meru Raya fire and rescue station was dispatched to the scene, 10km away, after receiving an emergency call at 5.14pm.
"A woman who was on the opposite bank of the river was rescued by firefighters, while a man who was on the riverbank was also rescued.
"Another male victim who was swept away managed to save himself from being carried away by the strong currents. All the survivors were in their 20s," he said in a statement tonight.
Sabarodzi said the search and rescue operation was focused on locating the missing woman, but the water current remained strong.
He said nine firefighters were involved in the search operation, with the assistance of various equipment and vehicles.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cardiothoracic services at Johor hospital unaffected despite department head's resignation
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Cardiothoracic services at Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA) remain unaffected and are operating as usual following the resignation of the department head on Monday.
HSA director Dr Mohamad Nizam Subahir said the cardiothoracic team continued to provide services in accordance with established clinical requirements.
"We respect his decision and record our appreciation for the contributions and commitment rendered.
"However, the resignation does not affect the continuity of cardiothoracic services to patients," he said in a statement.
Dr Nizam said hospital management had also taken note of allegations concerning operational issues and staffing requirements for the service.
He said management was aware of the matter and continued to address human resource needs to ensure the continuity and effectiveness of services.
"Efforts to improve and strengthen services are being undertaken in stages through discussions and coordination with the relevant parties," he said.
"Any decisions regarding operations, manpower deployment and cardiothoracic services are made based on collective discussion and consideration," he said.
Yesterday, a news portal reported that a doctor had resigned as the Johor Cardiothoracic Services head and Southern Zone cardiothoracic specialist, as well as head of the Cardiothoracic Surgery Department at HSA.
The resignations were submitted in two separate letters to Johor Health director Dr Mohtar Pungut and the HSA director on Monday, with immediate effect.
However, the doctor remains in service as a consultant cardiothoracic surgeon at HSA.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia foils attempts to smuggle 25.8kg of gold to Malaysia this month
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesian customs authorities have foiled three attempts this month to smuggle 25.8kg of gold worth an estimated 62.5 billion rupiah (RM14.06 million) to Malaysia.
One of the cases involved a Malaysian man who concealed gold bars in his shoes.
Teluk Bayur Customs and Excise Office head Ade Zirwan said the 34-year-old was detained at Minangkabau International Airport near Padang, West Sumatra, on Nov 12 for attempting to smuggle 4kg of gold worth an estimated 10 billion rupiah (RM2.25 million) out of Indonesia.
He said customs officers received information about a passenger displaying suspicious behaviour while monitoring the departure area for Malaysia-bound flights.
This prompted them to conduct further surveillance and checks.
"To follow up on the information, officers immediately conducted further surveillance and analysis of the passenger before carrying out an inspection," he said in a statement.
He added that laboratory tests confirmed the gold had a purity exceeding 99 per cent.
Ade said the suspect was detained for 20 days at the West Sumatra Police detention centre pending investigation into alleged violations of Indonesia's Customs Law, which carries a prison sentence of between one and 10 years and fines ranging from 50 million rupiah (RM12,500) to 5 billion rupiah (RM1.25 million) upon conviction.
In a separate statement, Indonesia's Directorate General of Customs and Excise said officers seized another 21.8 kilogrammes of gold worth an estimated 52.5 billion rupiah (RM11.80 million) in two cases involving passengers departing from Syamsudin Noor International Airport near Banjarmasin, South Kalimantan, on Nov 5 and 12.
In the first operation on Nov 5, the directorate said officers seized 4.2 kilogrammes of gold from four Indonesian women bound for Kuala Lumpur following X-ray baggage screening and body searches.
The items were taken to the Banjarmasin Customs Office for further examination.
In the second operation on Nov 12, three passengers preparing to board a flight to Kuala Lumpur were intercepted following passenger profiling. Officers discovered 17 gold bars weighing a total of 17.6 kilogrammes concealed inside their shorts and undershirts.
The directorate said the three passengers had been named as suspects and were undergoing customs investigations for allegedly attempting to export goods without submitting the required declarations.
It added that the two Banjarmasin seizures involved potential unpaid export duties of 5.2 billion rupiah (RM1.17 million).
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mascot-mad fans flock to meet-up of 200 characters in Japan
Article:
HANYU: Tens of thousands of mascot fans gathered in a city near Tokyo on Saturday to meet and greet more than 200 life-size cuddly characters promoting local towns and businesses.
In the land of Hello Kitty and Pokemon, mascots are used to promote everything from prisons and railways to private businesses, with popular ones gaining full-on celebrity status.
"This is the first time I've ever come to an event like this, so I'm kind of excited," Yuriko Okamori, 51, told AFP at the annual meet-up.
The mascot meet-up has been held in the city of Hanyu since 2010, and nearly 220 mascots were invited to join this year, according to organisers.
On a stage, a troupe of animal mascots danced to upbeat pop music as a large crowd filmed them on smartphones and clapped along.
Elsewhere, a popular pony mascot representing Gunma prefecture was surrounded by fans eager for selfies, while a cat mascot was pushed through the packed crowd on a cart to make its way across the venue.
[[nid:1582726]]
City official Shogo Dei, who oversees the event, said 80,000 people attended the two-day meet-up last year and that organisers expected a similar turnout this year.
"These local mascot characters representing regions are part of Japanese culture. Our aim is to help revitalise towns across Japan through these characters," Dei told AFP.
Mascots in Japan can generate millions of dollars in revenue if they become successful, even without the global recognition of major intellectual property brands such as Pikachu.
Another popular character, Hikonyan, a cat mascot wearing a samurai helmet and associated with Hikone Castle in western Japan, has helped draw tourists to the area. The character even received around 10,000 New Year's greeting cards from across Japan this January.
"There are so many different characters representing different places, and it's not uncommon to see even adults carrying mascot goods on their bags," Okamori said.
"I think that's something uniquely Japanese."
[[nid:1582725]]
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Maritime agency says two tankers struck in Hormuz as Iran says ship on fire
Article:
DUBAI: Two tankers were attacked on Saturday in the Strait of Hormuz, at the heart of the conflict between Iran and the United States, British maritime agency UKMTO said, as Iran reported that a ship was on fire.
"A tanker transiting outbound in the Strait of Hormuz has been hit on the stern by an unknown projectile. There are no reported casualties at this time," the agency said, adding that another tanker was struck in its engine room.
Since US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February launched the Middle East war, Teheran has sought to restrict passage through the strategic waterway and regularly targets ships that transit without its authorisation.
Iran's army on Saturday said a ship was on fire after hitting a mine in the strait.
"Before noon today, a violating oil tanker that had entered a restricted zone east of the Strait of Hormuz caught fire after striking a naval mine," Iran's army naval forces said in a statement carried by state TV.
The tanker "had its identification and navigation systems switched off, in defiance of issued warnings and maritime transit regulations," it added.
In recent weeks, Teheran has made multiple announcements saying ships have caught fire in the strait, often claiming they struck mines.
But the US military recently said it had cleared all mines from the main routes through the waterway.
Washington has responded to Iran's chokehold on the strait with a blockade of Iranian ports, and its navy has been escorting tankers through the waterway.
US Central Command, which oversees US military operations in the region, said last month that it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer.
Iran said on Saturday it had shot down a US drone over Qeshm Island in the strait, according to state TV.
American fighter jets struck an Iranian missile site on Qeshm last Tuesday, according to a US military official.
Before the onset of the Middle East war, one-fifth of the world's oil and natural gas passed through the Strait of Hormuz.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Negri Sembilan police yet to receive report from MB over resignation letter
Article:
SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan police have yet to receive a report from Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim over an alleged resignation letter submitted to the palace without his knowledge or consent.
Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad confirmed that Ismail had not lodged a police report so far.
"So far, there has been no report from the menteri besar," he said briefly when contacted.
Earlier today, Dang Wangi police chief Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin confirmed receiving a report over allegations that a letter of resignation by the Negri Sembilan menteri besar was submitted to the palace without his consent.
Azwan said the report was lodged by a
65-year-old male retiree
at the Chow Kit police station, under the Dang Wangi district police headquarters, around 9.55am today.
He said the complainant sought an investigation based on several media reports and statements.
The complainant also wanted police to investigate a possible link between the resignation letter issue and an alleged conspiracy against the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Wife of firefighter missing in Nepal harassed by debt collectors
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The wife of a senior fire officer reported missing in Nepal has spoken of the distress caused by repeated calls and threats from parties seeking to recover her husband's debts.
Hani Othman, 40, said she first received calls from an e-commerce platform company in October informing her that her husband, Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa, had outstanding payments.
"At the time, I explained the situation, including my husband's disappearance, and they asked me to submit the relevant documents via email.
"Although I had submitted the documents, I continued receiving calls threatening me with payment demands, even though I had already explained the circumstances," she said when contacted recently.
She said the calls had become increasingly frequent, with more than 10 calls a day from the parties involved.
"It's not that I don't want to settle the debt, but I am facing difficulties because I cannot access my husband's bank account to make the payments.
"They call me more than 10 times a day. I feel distressed when I am contacted and threatened over the debt every day," she said.
Hani said her husband did not have many outstanding debts, while his bank loan repayments had been granted a moratorium until February 2027.
"To be honest, I have come to terms with my husband's disappearance. However, I hope the families of others involved in the incident will have their affairs eased, including their financial matters.
"I believe many other families affected by the incident are facing similar problems, adding to the difficulties of managing their daily lives," she said.
She said the family was still waiting for official confirmation from the Nepalese authorities on her husband's status.
"Although DNA samples were submitted early in the incident, we have yet to receive an official announcement or written confirmation from the Nepalese authorities on the victims' status.
"I hope the government, particularly the Foreign Ministry, and the Nepalese authorities will continue efforts to find our loved ones.
"The lack of a definitive answer has left our status in limbo and prevented us from settling various important matters, including insurance claims and asset management," she said.
Fakhrul, 44, better known as Loe, was reported missing in Nepal following devastating floods in the country on Aug 26.
Also reported missing was Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department deputy director of the Fire and Rescue Operations Division, Mohd Sani Harul, who was part of the same climbing expedition.
According to the latest report by the Foreign Ministry (Wisma Putra), 54 Malaysians were still uncontactable, most of whom were believed to have been involved in climbing activities and expeditions in the affected areas.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 159 longhouse residents receive food aid as floods submerge ground floor
Article:
KUCHING: A total of 159 residents of a longhouse in the interior of Kapit received food supplies from firefighters after floodwaters submerged its entire ground floor to a depth of more than 2m today.
The 27-door John Kara longhouse in Kerangan was inundated, forcing residents to take shelter on the upper floor for their safety.
A Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department operations centre spokesman said the department received an emergency call about the flooding at 1.30pm.
He said a team from the Kapit Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched to monitor the situation and deliver food supplies to the affected residents.
"An operational team comprising four firefighters arrived at the location at 2.40pm after travelling 68km.
"Upon arrival, the operation commander conducted an initial assessment and confirmed that the entire ground floor of the longhouse had been submerged," he said.
An inspection found that floodwaters had risen to more than 2m on the ground floor, rendering the area uninhabitable.
However, no evacuation or rescue operation was necessary as all residents had already taken shelter on the upper floor.
Firefighters and personnel from other agencies subsequently monitored the situation and distributed food supplies to the affected residents.
After confirming that the situation was safe and under control, the team concluded its operation and returned to the station at 3.07pm.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Flood situation improves in Perak, Selangor; Negri Sembilan fully recovers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The number of flood evacuees in Perak and Selangor fell to 2,334 people from 683 families this afternoon, down from 2,368 people from 691 families this morning.
The flood situation in Negri Sembilan has also fully recovered, with its last temporary relief centre at SK Jimah closing at 2pm today, according to the Civil Defence Force.
In Perak, the number of evacuees at temporary evacuation centres in five districts dropped to 488 from 499 this morning.
The state Disaster Management Committee secretariat said an evacuation centre at SK Dato' Sagor in Perak Tengah, which housed 22 evacuees, was closed at 3pm today.
However, SK Tanjung Belanja remains open, sheltering 70 evacuees from 35 families.
The number of evacuees at the SRA Rakyat Padang Serai evacuation centre in Manjung remained unchanged at 131, from 39 families.
The Teluk Intan Municipal Council Rest House Hall in Hilir Perak is sheltering 97 evacuees from 31 families, while 10 people from four families remain at SK Batu Hampar in Larut, Matang and Selama.
In Kerian, 180 evacuees from 57 families, including 12 people from three families affected by a landslide, remain at SK Bukit Merah and SK Parit Haji Aman.
In Selangor, the Social Welfare Department's InfoBencana portal reported that the number of evacuees had fallen slightly to 1,846 from 1,869 this morning.
SK Dato' Maharaja Lela is sheltering the highest number of evacuees at 401, followed by SK Parit Mahang (365), SK Sultan Abdul Aziz (222), Sekolah Rendah Agama Bukit Kuching (216), Bukit Kuching Tengah Community Hall (139), SK Rantau Panjang (134) and SRA Batu 8 Ijok (120).
Other centres still operating are SK Jaya Setia, which is sheltering 98 evacuees, Kafa Integrasi Hidayah Bukit Cherakah (66), Seri Harmoni Community Hall (40), SK Batu Arang (25) and Kampung Sungai Kelambu Village Hall (20).
The Malaysian Meteorological Department forecast rain and thunderstorms in some parts of the state this afternoon, with conditions expected to clear by nightfall.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PKR open to PH parties using own logos in GE16
Article:
KUALA KANGSAR: PKR is not ruling out the possibility of Pakatan Harapan (PH) component parties using their respective logos in the 16th General Election (GE16), saying the proposal warrants consideration by the coalition's top leadership.
Its youth chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim said the proposal should be carefully examined in view of experience from previous elections and the current political landscape.
He said electoral success depended not only on the use of party logos but also on political strategy, track records in public service, engagement with the people and candidate selection.
"I do not deny that there is merit in the proposal and that specific considerations should be taken into account when reviewing our strategies and approaches.
"This matter needs to be examined carefully by the top leadership because winning an election is not just about the logo, but encompasses various aspects, including political strategy, service delivery, our approach to the people and the candidates themselves," he told reporters after the Hari Bertemu Komuniti and Study Assistance Handover programme at the Padang Rengas People's Community Centre.
Kamil was responding to a proposal for PH component parties, including PKR, DAP and Amanah, to use their respective logos in the next general election instead of a single coalition logo.
He said PKR had experience using its own logo in previous elections, which had never caused confusion among voters.
"PKR has been around for almost 30 years and we have seen that there has never been an issue in any election. In fact, we have used the PKR logo before.
"Indeed, the PKR logo made history when it helped PH win the 2018 general election," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump threatens to tax US firms that build data centres abroad
Article:
WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump threatened on Friday to impose a steep tax on US companies that build data centres overseas.
"We're not going to allow our companies to build data centres outside of our country," Trump told reporters at a White House briefing, reported German news agency dpa.
"If they do that, they can. But we're going to put a tremendous tax on them."
It was unclear what authority Trump could use to impose such a tax. Congress sets federal taxes, and Republicans are due to cede control of both chambers to Democrats in January.
Widespread public opposition to data centres in the US helped fuel the Democrats' election victory this month, but Trump has nevertheless remained a staunch supporter of the AI industry.
US companies have been building data centres abroad, including in Europe, for years.
Trump said he wanted more data centres constructed in the US, warning that if they were built abroad, "China will take all of them".
He said the United States was in a race with China to lead in artificial intelligence and argued that the winner would gain a broader advantage.
Trump said he and Chinese President Xi Jinping had agreed on some common safeguards for AI at their meeting this week in Shenzhen but gave no details.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent earlier told CNBC that the two sides had agreed that no major military operation should be launched without human involvement.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: South Korean president reiterates US$75,000 reward for reporting college exam cheating
Article:
SEOUL: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung reiterated on Saturday that the government would offer a reward of 100 million won (US$75,000) to anyone reporting cases of cheating in this week's college entrance examination, describing the misconduct as a "crime as serious as corruption" involving government officials, Yonhap News Agency reported.
Lee made the comments on social media, saying the reward would be paid for each case of cheating reported. This means the total reward could exceed 100 million won if someone reports multiple cases at once.
Lee also said that if a cheater turned themselves in and reported other accomplices, they would receive a reduced punishment for their offence while still receiving the full reward for reporting.
"Cheating on the college entrance exam is a crime as serious as corruption by public officials," Lee said. "We will track cheaters down to the very end and strictly punish exam cheating that steals the lifelong efforts of hundreds of thousands of test-takers."
Offering cash rewards is one of the anti-cheating measures the government has introduced amid growing concerns over the use of artificial intelligence (AI) during national examinations. The concerns followed an admission by this year's top scorer in the certified tax accountant examination that he had cheated with the help of AI and digital devices.
The concerns were further heightened by allegations that a 32-year-old man who scored full marks on the Legal Education Eligibility Test (LEET) had used AI to cheat. The man was found dead at a motel in Seoul on the day of the college entrance examination after failing to attend a live exam session he had promised to take to prove that he had not cheated.
The College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT), commonly known as Suneung, marks the culmination of years of rigorous study for many students and is widely regarded as a major life event in South Korea, where university admission can heavily influence career prospects.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Magnitude 6.8 earthquake strikes Banda Sea near Timor-Leste
Article:
BENGALURU: A magnitude 6.8 earthquake struck Banda Sea, 226km north-east of Dili, Timor-Leste on Saturday, the German Research Center for Geosciences (GFZ) said.
The quake was at a depth of 117km, GFZ said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cooperation with Thailand helps keep drugs out of Kelantan
Article:
KOTA BHARU: Kelantan police have maintained close cooperation with their Thai counterparts to curb cross-border criminal activities, particularly drug smuggling.
Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the cooperation had helped prevent prohibited substances, especially drugs, from entering the country through the state.
He said Thai authorities had also stepped up border security and planned to establish more checkpoints to tackle cross-border crime.
"We regularly cooperate and maintain contact with the Thai authorities, who have also been tightening security along the border.
"I was informed this morning that they would continue strengthening their border controls and introduce more posts, similar to what we are doing, to address cross-border crime.
"We thank the Thai authorities for helping to arrest drug traffickers and seize drugs before they can be brought into Malaysia, particularly Kelantan," he told reporters here today.
He was speaking after attending the Santai Anak Muda Bikers programme at the Kelantan police contingent headquarters here.
Yusoff also thanked Thai police for foiling a cross-border drug syndicate involving 750kg of methamphetamine, worth an estimated 300 million baht (RM36.3 million), believed to have been destined for Malaysia.
Thai authorities reportedly seized the drugs in Nakhon Si Thammarat province, about 150km north of Hat Yai, at 1.45am (Thai time) on Wednesday.
Two men, aged 31 and 40, were arrested along with a lorry allegedly used to transport the drugs.
The methamphetamine, packed in wrappers bearing the branding of a traditional Chinese tea, was found concealed beneath the lorry's floor panels, which had been modified to create a double-layered compartment.
The drugs were believed to have been transported from Chiang Rai province to Hat Yai district as a transit point before being smuggled into Malaysia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PN sees BN as most suitable partner for GE16
Article:
KUANTAN: Barisan Nasional (BN) appears to be the most suitable partner for Perikatan Nasional (PN), based on their electoral cooperation in Negri Sembilan and Melaka.
Wawasan secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Abdullah said the cooperation, dubbed the "Blue Wave", appeared to be gaining traction, particularly in the Negri Sembilan and Melaka state elections.
"There are two levels of cooperation. The first involves partners within the PN coalition, while the second entails political cooperation with any party deemed suitable to help the coalition form the federal government in Putrajaya.
"Based on our experience in Johor, Negri Sembilan and Melaka, BN is currently the most suitable partner," he told reporters after presenting his 2022-2026 parliamentary constituency report card.
Saifuddin said the current arrangement was referred to as the "Blue Wave" or "Muafakat BN-PN", but declined to elaborate, saying any decision on political cooperation would be made by the PN Supreme Council.
He said the council was expected to meet soon to review the outcome of the Negri Sembilan and Melaka state elections and discuss the coalition's future direction.
Asked about the possibility of extending the BN-PN partnership to the 16th general election (GE16), Saifuddin said the broader objective was to work with any party willing to cooperate to form the next federal government.
"This approach (BN-PN) appears to be working well in Negri Sembilan and Melaka. Johor was different, but in Negri Sembilan and Melaka, we adopted the 'Blue Wave' approach, which seems to be effective," he said.
On Nov 15, BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said there were no immediate plans to extend the
coalition's cooperation
with PN to GE16, although discussions remained possible if circumstances warranted it.
The BN-PN cooperation secured a two-thirds majority in the Negri Sembilan and Melaka state elections.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Perhilitan to set up camera traps to detect black panther in Sendayan
Article:
SEREMBAN: The Negri Sembilan Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) will install camera traps to detect a black panther after residents reported sightings in the Laman Sendayan residential area.
Its director, Wan Mat Wan Harun, said the move is to verify the complaint's authenticity before taking further action.
"The complaint location is about 12km from the Galah Permanent Forest Reserve (HSK).
"We received the report around 2pm today, and our team will set up camera traps this evening," he told Bernama here today.
He advised the public to exercise caution if they encounter the wild animal, avoid provoking it or taking matters into their own hands, and contact Perhilitan immediately for further action.
Earlier today, several photos uploaded by users on social media went viral, showing the animal roaming around, believed to be searching for food in the area.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Missing MCKK student found safe
Article:
IPOH: A 13-year-old Malay College Kuala Kangsar (MCKK) student who was reported missing yesterday was found safe in Taiping, four hours after police received a report on the disappearance.
Kuala Kangsar police chief Assistant Commissioner Heisham Harun said police received a report from the student's mother around 6pm after she was informed by the school that her child was missing.
He said police launched a search with the assistance of the Perak Criminal Investigation Department's Tracker Dog Unit (K9), as well as the school and family members.
"Following information provided by the public, the student was successfully located by the police in the Taiping district around 10pm and has been reunited with their parents in good and safe condition," he said in a statement.
Heisham said the incident was not connected, directly or indirectly, to the death of another student which was reported last Wednesday.
Earlier, a post went viral on social media about a Form One student from a boarding school in Kuala Kangsar who had been missing since yesterday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Four teens held after police chase near Simpang Pulai
Article:
IPOH: Police detained four teenagers, all under 15, for allegedly obstructing public servants from performing their duties at Km286.5 of the North-South Expressway northbound, near Simpang Pulai, yesterday.
Tapah deputy police chief deputy superintendent Mohd Fadzil Ismail said a team of policemen on patrol received information at 4.20pm from the district police headquarters control centre to assist Ringlet station personnel in tracking down a Toyota Chery multi-purpose vehicle occupied by several people suspected of being involved in a kidnapping case.
He said policemen then moved to Batu 3, Jalan Pahang, near Tapah, to conduct surveillance and spotted the vehicle about 5.30pm.
"Police instructed the driver to stop for inspection, but the driver failed to comply and instead sped off, nearly hitting an on-duty policeman.
"Police then chased the vehicle to the Tapah toll plaza. In an attempt to intercept it, the police vehicle's bumper was hit by the suspect's vehicle," he said in a statement today.
Fadzil said personnel from the Ipoh district police headquarters joined the chase before police intercepted the vehicle at Simpang Pulai.
He said all four suspects were arrested and the vehicle seized.
Initial investigations found that all four were teenagers, while urine screening tests showed they were drug-free and had no criminal records, he added.
"The three boys detained have been remanded for four days from today, while the girl was granted police bail as she is involved in an ongoing investigation in Jitra, Kedah," he said.
The case is being investigated under Sections 186, 279 and 353 of the Penal Code.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 25pc surge in patients causes congestion at Ampang Hospital
Article:
SHAH ALAM: A surge of up to 25 per cent above the daily average in patients seeking treatment at the Yellow Zone of Ampang Hospital's Emergency and Trauma Department has caused congestion and prolonged waiting times for ward admission.
The Selangor Health Department said the recent increase in patient numbers had also affected the smooth processing of admissions to the hospital's wards.
"The Emergency and Trauma Department at Ampang Hospital has seen a significant increase in patients at its Yellow Zone recently, with numbers rising by up to 25 per cent above the daily average.
"This has caused congestion at the department and affected the time taken for patients to be admitted to wards," it said in a statement.
The department said Ampang Hospital's management introduced several measures to address the congestion following the surge in patients.
This includes strengthening patient admission and discharge processes to ensure smoother patient flow.
"Additionally, the use of the discharge lounge has been expanded to improve efficiency, while ensuring human resource management is carried out effectively.
"The department appreciates public feedback and remains committed to ensuring optimal healthcare delivery without compromising patient safety and treatment management," it said.
It was reported that congestion at the hospital's Emergency Department, particularly the Yellow Zone, had left patients requiring further treatment waiting longer for ward beds.
Threads user @ayien78 claimed that almost every available space in the zone was occupied by beds and mobile beds to accommodate patients.
She also claimed that her father had been waiting for three days to be admitted to a ward but had yet to secure a bed due to overcrowding.
The situation not only left elderly patients waiting for extended periods but also placed a heavy burden on healthcare workers dealing with the high patient volume.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: No fake work pass syndicates detected in Kelantan, other border states
Article:
KOTA BARU: The Immigration Department has yet to detect any syndicates producing or distributing fake Temporary Employment Visit Passes (PLKS) in Kelantan or other states bordering Thailand.
Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said investigations so far had uncovered cases only in the Klang Valley.
He said the department would continue to monitor the situation closely.
"Although no such syndicate has been detected in the border states so far, our monitoring and surveillance efforts are ongoing," he said.
On Wednesday, Deputy Home Minister Datuk Seri Dr Shamsul Anuar Nasarah
told the Dewan Rakyat
that 36 Immigration Department officers and personnel had been detained, suspended or charged over a syndicate allegedly involved in issuing fake documents and Temporary Employment Visit Passes since 2025.
He said the action was taken through cooperation between the Home Ministry and the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC).
The agencies had also conducted several special operations, including Op Selat.
The 36 officers and personnel were detained, suspended or charged between 2025 and mid-2026.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysian man caught with 4kg gold hidden in shoes at Indonesian airport
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A Malaysian man was arrested after attempting to smuggle 4kg of gold worth about RM2.25 million hidden in his shoes at the Minangkabau International Airport in Padang, Indonesia.
The 34-year-old was detained at the departure area while preparing to board a flight to Malaysia on Nov 12.
Teluk Bayur Customs Office chief Ade Zirwan said the inspection was conducted with the assistance of airport security personnel.
"During monitoring, we received information about a passenger who was behaving suspiciously.
"Following this, officers carried out further surveillance and analysis before inspecting the passenger," he said in a statement published on the Indonesian Directorate General of Customs and Excise website.
Ade said the inspection uncovered four gold bars hidden in the man's shoes, with two bars concealed in each shoe.
He said tests using specialised detection equipment confirmed that the gold had a purity of more than 99 per cent and weighed about 4kgs in total.
"The gold was not declared to customs as required under regulations governing goods taken out of Indonesia.
"It also violated restrictions and prohibitions on goods being taken out of the country," he said.
He said the gold was estimated to be worth 10 billion rupiah (about RM2.25 million).
The man is being investigated under Section 102A of Law No. 17 of 2006 on Customs, which carries a jail term of between one and 10 years upon conviction.
The provision also carries a fine of between 50 million rupiah (about RM11,250) and five billion rupiah (about RM1.13 million).
"The suspect is currently being held for 20 days at the West Sumatra Regional Police detention centre, while all evidence has been seized for further legal action.
"We are also working with the West Sumatra Regional Police and Padang Pariaman Police to complete the investigation," he said.

Title: MOE studying need for more assistant wardens, counselling teachers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Education Ministry (MOE) is looking into the need to increase the number of assistant wardens and guidance and counselling teachers to ensure students receive optimal attention and support while staying in hostels.
Its minister, Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek, said the aspiration of parents to see their children gain admission to fully residential schools should be balanced with the children's own abilities and emotional readiness.
"As we plan for our children's future, it is important that we also listen to their voices and understand their feelings. Our dreams as parents must align with our children's own abilities and emotional readiness," she said in a Facebook post today.
Fadhlina said that she had held discussions with the police in Kuala Kangsar, Perak, on strengthening the safety and well-being of students residing in the hostel of the educational institution concerned.
The discussions covered compliance with standard operating procedures (SOPs), hostel management, and the importance of parents assessing their children's level of readiness before sending them to boarding schools.
She said every child had a different level of adaptability, with some adjusting quickly while others required more time, adding that some children were able to cope well with academic competition, while others needed greater encouragement.
As such, she said it was important to create an environment where children could share their thoughts and be heard without being judged.
"I want parents to know that we share the same hopes. We want our children to succeed, but more importantly, we want them to grow up safe and happy," she added.
She also advised parents not to be overly concerned if their children do not gain admission to their dream schools, as every child has his or her own unique path and timeline for achieving success.
"Most importantly, regardless of where they study, they must know that our love and acceptance never depend on the name of their school or their examination results," she added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mother devastated after losing two children in Sik fire
Article:
SIK: A 23-year-old mother was left devastated after her two children died in a fire at a former office building converted into a home in Kampung Teloi Tua here today.
The fire, which broke out around 6am, claimed the lives of siblings Aishah Umaira Abdul Latif, 16 months, and her 3-year-old brother, Mohd Raifal.
The children were found dead on a bed inside the premises.
The mother, who declined to be identified, said she realised the house was on fire when she returned, but could do nothing as the flames had spread rapidly.
The woman is believed to have returned to her hometown from Kuala Lumpur about two weeks ago and was staying with her father.
Police investigations found that the children had been living with their unemployed mother at their grandfather's home.
Meanwhile, Sik police chief Superintendent Shamzury Saman said a thorough investigation would be conducted, with statements to be recorded from all relevant parties, including the owner of the premises.
"The bodies were sent to the Forensic Department of Sultanah Bahiyah Hospital in Alor Star and post-mortems will be conducted tomorrow," he said.
It was reported today that a 16-month-old girl and a 3-year-old boy were killed in a fire at an office building converted into a home.
The victims were found
clinging
to each other on a mattress.

Title: Family escapes injury as car crashes into power pole, damaging house
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A family escaped injury after a car crashed into a power pole outside their home in Bandar Permas Jaya here, causing the pole to fall onto the roof and damage part of the house.
The 71-year-old homeowner, Ab Manaf Sujak, said he shuddered at the thought of what could have happened had the pole landed on the bedroom where his family was sleeping.
"I cannot imagine what would have happened to my family if the power pole had fallen on the bedroom," he said.
The chicken rice seller said his family was asleep when the incident occurred about 2am today. He woke up after hearing a loud crash and went outside to investigate.
"I was shocked to find the more than 5m-tall power pole had fallen onto the roof, damaging part of it. It also struck the boundary wall, a canopy beside the house and the front of a car.
"I also saw a car in the drain. Without hesitation, I went over and found that the driver was safe.
"The driver, who was in his 20s, claimed to have lost control of the car before crashing into the power pole and ending up in the drain," he said when contacted.
Ab Manaf said he was grateful that his 65-year-old wife and 20-year-old grandson, who were also at home, were unharmed.
"There have been several incidents of cars skidding into the drain in this area, but this is the first time one has caused damage to a house.
"I am at a loss over how to cover the cost of repairing the damage caused by the driver's negligence.
"The driver's family has met us and apologised for the incident.
"However, we are unsure whether they will bear the repair costs," he said.
Ab Manaf said he had lodged a report at the Johor Bahru Selatan District Traffic Police Station.
Photographs of the incident, showing the fallen power pole damaging the roof and boundary wall of the house, went viral on Threads from noon today.
The car was also seen in the drain.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Legal certainty key to public confidence in judiciary - Chief Justice
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Legal certainty is essential to maintaining public confidence in the judiciary, as citizens must be able to rely on the law when navigating legal matters and making decisions, said Chief Justice Tun Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh.
He said legal certainty was important because everyone appearing before a Malaysian court needed absolute clarity on what the law dictates and whether they could rely on it.
"Where the law is certain, people plan with confidence. Where it is not, they hesitate, they litigate, and they lose faith.
"A rule that cannot be known in advance cannot fairly be applied afterwards. Certainty is not a convenience of the legal system; it is a condition of justice. It is also a condition of trust," he said in his keynote address and official closing of the Malaysia Legal Forum 2026 at the Asian International Arbitration Centre.
The fourth edition of the Malaysia Legal Forum served as an annual platform for the country's legal fraternity to exchange views on landmark legal developments and discuss the future of the law in Malaysia.
Underscoring the importance of legal certainty, Justice Wan Ahmad Farid said it affected everyone, including investors, businesses, ordinary citizens, and accused persons, who required clarity on what the law dictated and whether it could be relied upon.
He said the judiciary had the responsibility to maintain a balance between fairness and legal certainty while operating within the boundaries of statutes and the Federal Constitution.
Using the children's story 'Goldilocks and the Three Bears' as an analogy, he said lawmakers, regulators, practitioners, and judges were constantly searching for an elusive balance that was just right within the legal system.
Citing artificial intelligence as an example, Wan Ahmad Farid said excessive regulation could stifle innovation and drive businesses away, while inadequate or outdated rules could leave society exposed to algorithmic abuse, corporate misconduct and fraud.
"Independence exists for only this purpose. It is not for our comfort, but so that the public can rely on a law that does not shift with the winds.
"The true art of the law lies in finding that magic spot where commercial pragmatism meets constitutional principle, where technological speed meets human conscience, and where efficiency never sacrifices fairness," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Air Niugini flight lands safely in Philippines after emergency
Article:
MANILA: An Air Niugini plane carrying 146 passengers and crew from Hong Kong to Papua New Guinea made an emergency landing safely on Saturday in a southern Philippine city after an indication of a possible engine fire, Philippine aviation officials said.
There were no reports of injuries among the 137 passengers and nine crew members, who disembarked using emergency slides from the Boeing 767-383ER after it diverted from its route and landed at Davao International Airport, the Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines said, according to AP.
The pilots reported detecting possible sparks or fire in the right engine through an indicator.
They followed safety procedures and requested an unscheduled landing in Davao shortly after midnight, Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines spokesperson Eric Apolonio said, without elaborating. He added that an investigation would include the pilots' accounts.
The passengers and crew were taken to the airport terminal and provided with assistance and hotel accommodation. There were no immediate reports of damage to the plane.
Davao airport was closed to other flights to allow emergency response, causing two incoming domestic flights to be cancelled. It was reopened later after safety checks were completed on the main runway, according to the Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines.

Title: MCA leaves Negri Sembilan crisis decisions to BN leadership
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MCA is leaving it to the Barisan Nasional top leadership to decide on the party's position in the ongoing crisis involving the royal institution and state administration in Negri Sembilan.
MCA deputy president Datuk Dr Mah Hang Soon said the party had not issued any specific instructions to its assemblymen so far.
"I think it is clear that we are standing with the BN top leadership.
"The actions taken and developments so far also clearly reflect that position," he told a press conference after officiating the 2026 MCA Youth Annual General Assembly.
The crisis in Negri Sembilan,
which began in April, escalated when the Undang Yang Empat, including three whose positions are disputed, and the Tunku Besar of Tampin announced the removal of Tuanku Muhriz and named Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Jaafar as the state's 12th Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
Meanwhile, in his speech at the assembly, Mah said MCA's cooperation with other parties should be assessed pragmatically.
He said political cooperation was not the exclusive right of any political party and that the public should apply the same standards when evaluating strategic alliances between parties.
"Throughout this time, DAP has defended its cooperation with other parties on pragmatic grounds.
"Therefore, the strategic cooperation of other parties, including MCA, must also be judged by the same standards," he said.
He said MCA would not blindly accept every decision when working with other parties, but would continue to assess them critically.
"We can cooperate without losing our own voice. We can support stability, but we must not allow any weaknesses in governance to escape scrutiny.
"MCA cannot become a party that merely nods and agrees. We must have our own position, capability and courage to defend it," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Armizan: GRS to decide GE16 direction collectively
Article:
PAPAR: Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) has yet to decide on the form of political cooperation for the 16th general election (GE16) and the matter has been left to the coalition's Supreme Council to discuss and decide upon collectively when the time is right.
GRS secretary-general Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said any decision must take into account the views of component parties which reflect the voices of members at the grassroots as well as the signals sent by the public during the 2025 Sabah state election.
He said the objective of establishing a stable government at both the federal and state levels to ensure smooth administration and the effective delivery of services to the people is a key factor in determining the coalition's political direction.
"Regarding core issues and policies concerning cooperation and political direction, my personal views are not what matters, what is important are the deliberations and decisions made collectively by the leadership through the GRS Supreme Council," he told reporters after launching the 'Disaster Preparedness: Amateur Radio as Alternative Communication' programme for Sabah state level.
Armizan, who is also domestic trade and cost of living minister, said GRS is currently focused on strengthening its position across all constituencies.
He made these remarks when asked to comment on a proposal for GRS to cooperate with Barisan Nasional (BN) under the Muafakat Sabah framework, a suggestion recently raised by Tenom Umno division chief Datuk Raime Unggi as well as the possibility of continuing the existing cooperation with Pakatan Harapan (PH).
Armizan said every political party has the right to determine its own direction heading into an election, and he does not intend to comment on the stances of other parties.
However, he said, GRS is open to political cooperation drawing on the coalition's past experience of working with other parties, both before and after the previous Sabah state election, to ensure the stability of the state administration.
He said this experience with political cooperation, alongside feedback from component party members and signals from voters in the Sabah state election, will be key factors considered before a collective decision is reached regarding GRS's direction for the GE16.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sabah community-based tourism generates RM7mil in 2025
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Community-based tourism in Sabah generated more than RM7 million in revenue in 2025, with visitor arrivals rising 23.3 per cent to 362,141 from 293,623 in 2024.
Sabah Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister Datuk Jafry Ariffin said the figures reflected its potential to generate income for communities and support the rural economy.
"These figures reflect the potential of community-based tourism and the importance of strengthening community participation, product quality and sustainable practices," he said at the opening of the three-day Sabah Community-Based Tourism Fair 2026 at Suria Sabah.
He said the state aimed to ensure that all registered community-based tourism and homestay products in Sabah met the relevant Asean standards by 2030.
Sabah currently has 13 community tourism and homestay products listed under the Asean tourism standard awards, covering community-based tourism, homestays and sustainable tourism.
Another five products have received recognition under the national-level Asean standards programme for 2025 to 2027.
Jafry said the state would use Visit Sabah Year 2027 to promote more local tourism experiences, including cultural activities, traditional handicrafts, agrotourism, local food and nature-based activities.
He said promotional efforts should go beyond well-known attractions to encourage visitors to explore more rural destinations.
He also called on industry players to include more community-based products in their tour packages and itineraries to ensure rural communities benefited from the expected increase in visitors.
On complaints that diving packages and accommodation in
Semporna
were becoming more expensive than those at international destinations, Jafry said he had yet to receive an official report.
"I have not yet received any official report on this matter. However, if there is indeed such an issue, I believe it could be attributed to fuel supply and consumption costs," he said.
In Semporna, particularly on the islands, fuel was essential as boats were used to travel between islands, he said.
Similarly, islands without electricity had to rely on fuel for their energy needs, resulting in high fuel consumption, he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: First ECRL ride? It’s your chance to explore some East Coast attractions and sample some great local eats
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 — Beyond the platforms of the three main East Coast terminal stations is a variety of local food, cultural attractions and leisure activities awaiting travellers on board the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL).
This really is the perfect opportunity to explore what Pahang, Terengganu and Kelantan have to offer.
KotaSAS
The first major stop is KotaSAS Station in Pahang, located approximately eight kilometres from Indera Mahkota, a suburb of Kuantan, and 10 kilometres from the city centre.
It serves as the main Express stop for the state capital, with the journey from Terminal Bersepadu Gombak taking approximately one hour and 35 minutes.
KotaSAS, also known as Kota Sultan Ahmad Shah, is Pahang’s new state administrative centre, comprising a planned township of government buildings, residential developments and commercial areas on the western outskirts of Kuantan.
For visitors, the station serves as a gateway to Kuantan which lies along the Kuantan River near the South China Sea.
Travellers can get around Kuantan using e-hailing services such as Grab or the Bas.my city bus network.
Restoran Satay Zul is among Kuantan’s best-known eateries offering grilled chicken, beef, rabbit and venison skewers every evening until around midnight.
Another local favourite is Restoran Akob Patin House, known for its ikan patin masak tempoyak (catfish cooked in fermented durian gravy).
Teluk Cempedak is a popular beach located approximately five kilometres east of Kuantan city centre and about 15 kilometres from KotaSAS Station.
Another attraction worth visiting is Kuantan 188, a 188-metre observation tower situated along the banks of the Kuantan River. It is the tallest tower on the East Coast of Peninsular Malaysia and the country’s second-tallest observation tower, after KL Tower.
Kuala Terengganu
The second major stop is Kuala Terengganu Station in Terengganu, approximately 8.7 kilometres from Bukit Payong, a suburb of Kuala Terengganu and 23 kilometres from the city centre.
It serves as the main Express stop for the state capital, with the journey taking approximately one hour and 25 minutes from KotaSAS, or two hours and 52 minutes from Terminal Bersepadu Gombak.
Kuala Terengganu sits at the mouth of the Terengganu River and is known for traditional boat-building, batik and songket.
With no feeder bus service yet, travellers can use e-hailing services such as Grab, take a taxi or rent a car to get around the city.
For a taste of classic Terengganu cuisine, head to Restoran Nasi Dagang Atas Tol, where the signature nasi dagang features rice steamed with coconut milk and served with fish curry.
Travellers can also sample nasi kerabu, another local favourite featuring blue-tinted rice served with a mixture of finely sliced herbs and vegetables, paired with various dishes at Suerasa Nasi Kerabu in the city.
Reflecting the city’s Islamic heritage, there are two mosques here, each with its own distinctive appeal, which are worth a visit.
One is the Crystal Mosque, or Masjid Kristal, which stands out for its sleek, modern design, incorporating steel, glass and crystal; the other is the Tengku Tengah Zaharah Mosque (Floating Mosque), the first floating mosque in Malaysia.
Kota Bharu
The third and final stop is Kota Bahru Station in Kelantan, approximately 9.2 kilometres from the city centre.
It serves as the main Express stop for the state capital, with the journey taking approximately one hour from Kuala Terengganu, or three hours and 52 minutes from Terminal Bersepadu Gombak.
Kota Bharu, which sits near the mouth of the Kelantan River, is known for its traditional crafts as well as its distinctive culinary offerings.
While a new terminal has yet to be built adjacent to the ECRL station, travellers can use Grab, take a taxi or rent a car to get around the city.
For a taste of the famed roti titab, travellers can head to Kopitiam Kita, where the dish originated. It features thick slices of bread toasted with butter, topped with kaya and a runny half-boiled egg.
Then there is nasi Kak Wok, a popular mixed rice dish said to have originated in Kota Bharu, at Nasi Kak Wok Lundang, located behind Kota Bharu Medical Centre along Jalan Dato Panglima Perang.
The eatery is among the local spots associated with the dish’s late founder, Mek Wook Hassan, fondly known as “Kak Wook”.
In the city, travellers can visit Pasar Besar Siti Khadijah, a vibrant market known for its predominantly female traders, while Istana Jahar and the surrounding heritage quarter offer a glimpse into the history of Kelantan’s royal court.

Title: Accountant finds stress relief in origami, turns 1,111 paper folds into eye-catching 3D arch
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 — Spending her days immersed in figures and financial statements has not stopped an accountant from expressing her creative side through the art of paper folding, or origami, with her three-dimensional (3D) craft creations attracting considerable attention.
For Wan Nur Saaraa Wan Manshol, the traditional Japanese art form, which she has been practising for more than 30 years, is more than just a hobby to fill her leisure time. It has also become a form of therapy to calm her mind and relieve stress after a hectic day at work.
What began as a way to relax has since evolved into something more remarkable, with the 45-year-old successfully creating a 3D origami arch using 1,111 origami units, showcasing how the art form can be transformed into unique and creative decorative pieces.
Known as the Kusudama Arch, the creation, made using the Kusudama Sonobe technique and comprising 38 paper balls of various sizes and 151 heart-shaped ornaments, attracted visitors’ attention during the World Origami Day celebration held here recently.
“Last year, I made a lampshade using paper, but this time I wanted to try something different by creating an arch. I wanted to show that origami can also be used as an attractive decorative element, especially in 3D form,” she told Bernama.
Met at the exhibition recently, Wan Nur Saaraa said that besides the creation, which took a week to complete, she had also showcased several other works, including Sonobe Light Haven, The Sonobe Lucky Cat, Songket in Fold and Batik in Love Fold.
Wan Nur Saaraa, who is affiliated with the Malaysia Origami Academy and has no intention of turning the art into a source of supplementary income, said origami had similarities with her profession as an accountant, as both required precision and balance.
“As an accountant, every account must balance. It is the same with origami. If the folds are not balanced, the final shape will not look beautiful. There is a different sense of satisfaction when I successfully complete a piece, and it helps relieve stress. It is the most affordable hobby.
“All you need is paper. Newspapers or paper bags can also be used, as long as you have patience and precision. I hope more people will give it a try because it can help sharpen creativity and calm the mind,” she said, adding that she hoped to create larger and more challenging origami pieces in the future.
Meanwhile, for Naqeeb Mateen Mohamad Najmuddin, 9, paper folding is an enjoyable activity that allows him to create various animal shapes, including snakes, Godzilla, fish, crabs and parrots.
“Because it looks cool,” said the Year 2C student at the Malaysia Origami Academy.
Elaborating further, his mother, Harizah Hanim Mohamed, said her eldest son’s interest began last year after he became fascinated by the various shapes that could be created through the craft, which he initially learnt by watching videos on YouTube.
This prompted her and her husband to enrol Naqeeb Mateen in origami classes early this year to nurture his interest and talent in paper folding, as the boy was less inclined towards sports activities.
“Since joining the academy, he has become more focused because origami is like mathematics, teaching children to understand each folding step carefully. Participating in exhibitions also helps build his courage and self-confidence,” she said. — Bernama

Title: From factory floor to AI, Micron Malaysia employees chart career paths through skills development
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 —  From starting as an operator to training others, and from working in component assembly to exploring artificial intelligence (AI), employees at Micron Malaysia are building their skills and advancing their careers as manufacturing processes become increasingly sophisticated.
Nor Shamim Mat Saffar, who joined Micron as an operator in 2019, has completed Levels 2 and 3 of the Malaysian Skills Certificate (SKM) and progressed to training others.
Her initial work in surface mount technology front-of-line operations provided a foundation in manufacturing, safety, quality and adherence to standard operating procedures.
“Don’t be afraid to start as an operator. I started as an operator myself, and that was where I built the foundation of my career. Keep learning, build your skills and don’t be afraid to take opportunities when they come your way,” she said in a statement.
Nor Shamim hopes to pursue a diploma and eventually take on a supervisory role, while the company’s shift arrangements help her balance work and family responsibilities.
Another employee, process engineer Kevin Lee Kar Heng, who joined Micron in January 2021 in the component assembly team, has been involved in Autonomous Defect Classification, which uses AI to support automated defect screening.
He has also used generative AI tools to accelerate his learning, including while developing a Power BI dashboard.
“For me, engineering is a bit like detective work. You see a problem, you look at the data, figure out what’s happening and try to solve it. That’s the part I enjoy. And now with AI, there are so many more things we can try and learn,” he said.
Lee’s professional development has extended to technical papers, research collaborations and conference participation, alongside leadership in initiatives under the Mosaic employee resource group.
He also values Micron’s management and technical career pathways, which enable technical contributors to progress while remaining close to the work they enjoy.
“Going forward, I want to keep challenging myself, take on bigger problems and continue growing, while staying close to the technical work that I enjoy.
“We should give ourselves the chance to explore. That’s how you discover what really fits you. Ultimately, passion and personal fit are often discovered by doing, not simply by thinking about them,” he said.
Micron Malaysia said its investment in employees encompasses AI upskilling, skills development and programmes supporting graduates and future leaders.
“As manufacturing becomes more sophisticated, team members have opportunities to build capabilities in areas including advanced manufacturing, automation, data analytics, AI-enabled processes, engineering, quality and reliability,” it said.
The company said its teams support leading-edge assembly and testing across solid-state drives, NAND flash memory, dynamic random-access memory for personal computers (PCDRAM) and memory modules, alongside product qualification and engineering.
This includes its world-first high-capacity 256GB low-power dynamic random-access memory (LPDRAM) SOCAMM2 module, produced in Penang for next-generation AI data centre infrastructure.
The company said the value of AI is about more than speed, as it also enables employees to learn, experiment and share knowledge so that more people can contribute to innovation.
Micron Malaysia said its investment in employees extends beyond skills and career development through its Total Rewards approach, which recognises contributions through competitive compensation and performance-based rewards.
Eligible employees also have opportunities to share in the company’s long-term growth.
The company said its wellbeing approach spans physical, mental, social, career and financial wellbeing to support employees across different aspects of their working lives.
In Malaysia, initiatives include health and wellness coverage, meal subsidies, confidential counselling and employee advocacy resources, alongside continued improvements to workplace facilities and experiences.
Micron established its operations in Muar, Johor, in 2010 before making a greenfield investment in Penang in 2018, developing its memory and storage manufacturing capabilities, engineering expertise and talent in Malaysia. — Bernama

Title: Kedah records 406 fatal motorcycle accidents in 10 months, 72 involving under-18 riders
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Nov 20 — A total of 406 fatal accidents involving motorcycles were recorded in Kedah between January and October this year, with 72 of these cases involving riders under the age of 18.
Kedah police contingent headquarters (IPK) Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department (JSPT) chief, Superintendent Abdel Nasser S. Salleh, said these statistics indicate that the safety of motorcyclists particularly teenagers requires serious attention.
He emphasised that the police take a stern view of unauthorised modification of motorcycles which deviates from established specifications as well as “street hooliganism” (reckless riding/illegal racing), as these actions not only endanger the riders themselves but also pose a threat to other road users.
“Seized motorcycles may be reclaimed, subject to compliance with stipulated terms and procedures including replacing non-compliant components with original parts or approved standard components,” he said in a statement here today.
He added that the police would ensure the release process for these motorcycles is carried out in accordance with prevailing legal provisions.
Abdel Nasser said enforcement efforts will continue to be intensified to ensure that road users adhere to established laws and regulations.
He also urged the public especially the youth and parents to play their part in ensuring that the motorcycles being used are kept in a safe condition and comply with the required specifications.
“Do not turn public roads into a racetrack. Make safety your top priority,” he said.
For the record, 3,282 motorcycles have been seized across Kedah during the same period, as part of ongoing enforcement operations conducted throughout the state.
Among the violations detected were modifications to motorcycle components that did not comply with established specifications including the exhaust, swingarm, rims, and other parts. — Bernama

Title: Man who posed as Selangor royal aide gets 27 more months’ jail, two strokes of cane for vehicle scam
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 20 — A man who impersonated an Aide-de-Camp (ADC) to the Raja Muda of Selangor and had been sentenced to imprisonment for fraud involving property and luxury vehicle purchases was sentenced to another 27 months’ imprisonment and two strokes of the cane today for similar offences.
Today, Al Zulfadly Alias, 40, was sentenced by the Magistrate’s Court here to a total of 27 months’ imprisonment and two strokes of the cane for cheating two victims of RM73,000 in a vehicle auction scam.
Magistrate Wan Noora Nisa Ngadirin meted out the jail sentence and fine after Al Zulfadly pleaded guilty to the charges.
The court ordered the prison terms to run consecutively, effective from the dates he was charged with the offences.
Meanwhile, Al Zulfadly’s fiancée, Nurul Nur Syahirah Kamarudin, 37, pleaded not guilty to the same charges. The court fixed Jan 19, 2027, for mention.
Today’s proceedings focused on the presentation of facts in Al Zulfadly’s case and the sentencing.
The couple was accused of conspiring with a 43-year-old man to deceive a 48-year-old man by falsely claiming they could facilitate the purchase of a used Honda CR-V, purportedly acquired through an auction held in conjunction with the ASEAN Summit, for RM33,000.
The offence was allegedly committed at a premises here between May 13 and 14.
The charge was framed under Section 109 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 420 of the same Code, which provides for a maximum jail term of 10 years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.
Al Zulfadly was sentenced to 12 months’ imprisonment and one stroke of the cane for the offence.
The couple was also jointly charged with deceiving a 43-year-old woman by claiming they could facilitate the purchase of a used Lexus RX350, purportedly acquired through an auction held in conjunction with the ASEAN Summit, for RM40,000.
The offence, framed under Section 420 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34, was allegedly committed at a premises in Taman Sri Andalas here between April 13 and 14.
Al Zulfadly was sentenced to 15 months’ imprisonment and one stroke of the cane for the offence.
According to the case facts, the male victim met the couple at a restaurant to obtain information about the sale of used vehicles in conjunction with the ASEAN Summit.
During the meeting, Al Zulfadly introduced himself as an ADC to the Raja Muda of Selangor and claimed he could arrange the purchase of vehicles through an auction.
He allegedly used his purported position to convince both victims that he could secure vehicles for them at lower prices.
Believing his claims, the victims transferred RM33,000 and RM40,000, respectively, into a bank account belonging to Al Zulfadly. However, neither received the vehicles as promised.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Nur Amirah Zahari urged the court to order the prison terms to run consecutively, citing the seriousness of the offences, particularly the impersonation of an ADC to the Raja Muda of Selangor.
“The accused deceived two complainants, who believed he possessed the influence to facilitate the purchase of vehicles. This severe sentence serves as a clear message to the public that the court views such offences with the utmost seriousness and will not compromise with those who break the law.
“It is also hoped that this sentence will serve as a lesson to both the accused and the public, as a deterrent against similar offences,” she said.
However, Al Zulfadly’s lawyer, Yong Kum Lam, from the National Legal Aid Foundation (YBGK), appealed for a lighter sentence, saying his client was unemployed and remorseful.
The couple was initially charged at the Shah Alam Magistrate’s Court on Nov 12 with cheating involving the sale of an auctioned vehicle worth RM33,000.
The following day, Nov 13, they were charged at the Klang Magistrate’s Court over the RM40,000 vehicle scam. The case was subsequently transferred to the Shah Alam court.
On Nov 16, Al Zulfadly was sentenced to one year’s imprisonment and two strokes of the cane by the Kuala Lumpur Magistrate’s Court after pleading guilty to cheating a celebrity in a property purchase scam.
The following day, he was sentenced by the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court to two years’ imprisonment and four strokes of the cane after being convicted on four counts of cheating a female doctor of RM155,000 involving property and luxury vehicle purchases. — Bernama

Title: Police seize RM1.27m in health, cosmetic and food products in Banting raid, three held
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 20 — Police detained three individuals and seized health, cosmetic and food products worth RM1.27 million during a raid at a logistics premises in Banting, Selangor yesterday.
The operation, codenamed Op Taring Dosej, was carried out at 12.10 pm by the Wildlife Crime Bureau/Special Intelligence Investigation (WCB/PSK) under the Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department (JKDNKA), together with several enforcement agencies.
Bukit Aman JKDNKA WCB/PSK commander SAC Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar said those detained comprised a local man believed to be the company owner and two Bangladeshi men employed at the premises.
He said checks found 1,044 boxes of health and cosmetic products, 1,300 bottles of supplements and health products, 38 boxes of pure tremella soup products, 65 boxes of coenzyme Q10 products and various tea-based food and beverage items and snacks.
“All the seized items have been handed over to the respective enforcement agencies for further action and investigation under their respective jurisdictions,” he said in a statement today.
The total value of the seizure is estimated at RM1.27 million. The Ministry of Health (MOH) recorded the highest seizure value at RM1.26 million, followed by the Kuala Langat District Health Office at RM5,167 and the Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN) at RM4,745.
Also participating in the operation were the MOH Selangor State Pharmacy Division, KPDN, the Royal Malaysian Customs Department Klang Branch, the Kuala Langat District Health Office and the Kuala Langat Municipal Council (MPKL).
In the same operation, the Kuala Langat District Health Office issued two compounds totalling RM4,500. MPKL issued two compounds amounting to RM2,000.
The case is being investigated under the Immigration Act 1959/63, the Control of Drugs and Cosmetics Regulations 1984, the Trade Descriptions Act 2011, the Food Act 1983 and related regulations.
Mohd Zaki said police would continue to strengthen enforcement and intelligence operations to address smuggling and the distribution of illicit goods. — Bernama

Title: Lorry driver in Sabah to face trial in April 2027 over alleged sexual offence against stepdaughter, 16
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Nov 20 — A 33-year-old lorry driver charged with committing physical sexual harassment against his stepdaughter, will go trial on April 7 and 8, 2027.
Sessions Court Judge Zaini Fishir set the date for the man whose case was brought up for pre-trial case management to serve all the relevant documents.
The man is accused of committing the offence by fondling the breasts of the 16-year and ten-month-old girl for the purpose of sexual at 5am August 22 this year at a house in Tuaran.
The offence under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, carries a jail term of up to 20 years and whipping upon conviction.
The court had released the man on bail of RM10,000 with RM5,000 deposited in two local sureties after granting his application of bail through his counsel.
The man also was ordered to report to Kundasang police station once a month pending the disposal of his case.
Earlier, counsel Jagnesh Jaya who defended the man, applied for bail to be granted as in previous proceedings in Tuaran Sessions Court, the man was not granted bail.
Jagnesh told the court that the man who has four children, has no counsel at that time he was charged in court and asked for a lower bail.
However, Deputy Public Prosecutor Fazriel Fardiansyah Abdul Kadir objected the application but if the court allow the application, Fazriel had suggested the bail sum of RM10,000.
Meanwhile, a 42-year-old man was fined RM100 or seven days’ jail for failing to explain how he had in possession the three packets of instant drinks believed to be stolen.
Azmi Mohd Ayub@ Md Ayub pleaded guilty before Magistrate Dzul Helmy Yunus, to failing to give reasonable explanation about the instant drinks at 11pm on November 12 this year at a supermarket in Lido, Penampang. — Daily Express

Title: ‘Qibla marker’ on Mount Kinabalu is a prayer aid, not a religious privilege, says Sabah mufti
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Nov 20 — The provision of a qibla (direction of prayer) marker on Mount Kinabalu is a basic facility for Muslims to perform prayers and is not intended to grant exclusive rights to any religion, said Sabah Mufti Datuk Dr Bungsu @ Aziz Jaafar.
In a statement today, he explained that the presence of the marker indicating the direction of Kaabah did not mean that the rights of followers of other religions to practise their respective faiths on the mountain were being denied or sidelined.
“The presence of the qibla marker does not in any way prevent followers of other religions from praying or practising their respective faiths on the mountain.
“There is no such thing as exclusive privileges for any particular religion on Mount Kinabalu,” he said, adding that anyone could engage in religious activities, subject to their needs and approval from Sabah Parks.
Bungsu said the installation of a qibla marker was also not carried out arbitrarily, as it required official verification from an authorised body such as the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim) or the relevant religious department to ensure its directional accuracy.
He said followers of other religions, including Christians, Hindus, Buddhists and those of other faiths, are welcomed to submit proposals for specific facilities to Sabah Parks management for consideration, subject to suitability and park regulations.
On the issue of fairness to followers of all religions, he explained that equal treatment should not be measured by providing identical facilities for all religious practices. Instead, it should ensure that every visitor is respected and given the space to practise their faith without infringing on the rights of others.
“The public should not confuse the provision of facilities for one religion with granting privileges that deny the rights of other religions, as the qibla marker is merely a directional guide and facility, not an obligation,” he said.
However, he stressed that safety and compliance with the standard operating procedures (SOP) for climbing activities remained the absolute priority and must not be compromised by any religious or cultural activities.
He also reminded the public that Mount Kinabalu remained open to all segments of society, and that the responsibility of safeguarding the safety and sustainability of the natural treasure must be shared by everyone.
Previously, the installation of a qibla direction marker on Mount Kinabalu went viral on social media, becoming a topic of discussion among netizens. — Bernama

Title: Negeri Sembilan MB disowns resignation letter submitted to Tuanku Muhriz
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 20 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has clarified that he never authorised the submission of his resignation letter to Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, contrary to reports on Monday.
He said the letter had been kept by the party leadership but stressed that he had never consented to its submission under such circumstances.
“I did not personally submit the resignation letter to His Royal Highness. The letter was indeed kept by the party leadership, but I never agreed to it being submitted in that manner.
“I only learnt about it through social media, and His Royal Highness also did not accept the way it was done. I neither submitted nor consented to the letter being presented to His Royal Highness. I do not even know who delivered it,” he told a press conference at the Menteri Besar’s official residence here today.
Earlier, Ismail was granted an audience with Tuanku Muhriz at Istana Hinggap, which was also attended by Undang Luak Rembau Datuk Sedia Raja Datuk Hassan Ab Hamid, Undang Luak Sungai Ujong Datuk Klana Petra Datuk Muhammad Faris Johari and Undang Luak Jelebu Datuk Mendika Menteri Akhirulzaman Datuk Azrin Khairi.
Following the audience, Ismail, who is also Juasseh assemblyman, said Tuanku Muhriz had decreed that he continue serving as Menteri Besar to ensure continuity in the state administration.
